17 The force resisting the motion of a car is proportional to the square of the car’s speed. The
magnitude of the force at a speed of 20.0 m s–1 is 800 N.
What useful output power is required from the car’s engine to maintain a steady speed of
40.0 m s–1?
A
32 kW
B
64 kW
C
128 kW
D
512 kW

hints: Notice the speed increases from $20.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$ to $40.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$, a factor of 2, while the resistive force is proportional to $v^2$.
Connect steady speed to balanced forces, so engine driving force equals the new resistive force, and useful power follows $P = Fv$.
First work out the new resistive force by multiplying $800\text{ N}$ by $2^2$, then multiply that force by $40.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and convert to $\text{kW}$.
walkthrough: Identify the given data: $F = 800\text{ N}$ at $v = 20.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$, with $F$ proportional to $v^2$, and the target speed is $40.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Use the $v^2$ proportionality to scale the force. Speed ratio is $40.0/20.0 = 2$, so force ratio is $2^2 = 4$.
Calculate the new resistive force: $F_{new} = 800 \times 4 = 3200\text{ N}$.
For steady speed the engine driving force must equal the resistive force, so $F_{drive} = 3200\text{ N}$.
Convert to kilowatts: $128000\text{ W} = 128\text{ kW}$. This is option C.

A.explanation: 32 kW is too small because it assumes power only doubles when speed doubles from $20.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$ to $40.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$, ignoring the $v^2$ rise in force.

B.explanation: 64 kW is the power at $20.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$ from $800 \times 20.0$, not the power after both force and speed increase at $40.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

C.explanation: At $40.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$ the resistive force is $3200\text{ N}$ and $P = Fv = 128000\text{ W} = 128\text{ kW}$.

D.explanation: 512 kW assumes power is proportional to $v^4$ with a factor of 8 from force times a factor of 8, rather than force up by 4 and speed up by 2.
